title: Spano's tonk: piano, chair drumming and the dancing women
summary: Nash describes Spano's at Liberty and Perdido, the old songs played and the grizzly bear, snatch bite and eagle rock dances.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Spano's tunk was at Libra and Perdida. And a guy playing the piano in there. Another guy beating the drumsticks on the chair, on the hard chair. And the folks at the outside would hear the music. They'd bust in there. Sometime I had much as 15, 20 women in there. And start dancing. While the guys playing the old songs of New Orleans. They used to play such as old numbers like Stagger Lee. And they used to do all those old numbers like Winter Night. Junk Man Rag. Bacer Street. St. Burst Blues. Long Ways Tipper Wherry. Yes, We Have No Bananas. Steamboat Bill. K.C. John and all those numbers. At that time it was very popular.
What kind of dance did the women do?
Well, they was doing a dance you call the bear at that time. The bear? Yeah, they were doing the bear, the grizzly bear.

Well, they'd jump back and shift forward. They'd walk like a bear. Like a bear? Sometimes a guy would get out on his hand and walk on his hand and jump back on his feet and sort of walking. They called it the, in other words, the name of the entire dance was the grizzly bear, what it was. Used to do.

The deer? Yeah. The grizzly bear. Then they would do the, they would do this dance they called the snatch bite. The snatch bite. Then they would do another dance they called the eagle rock. Rock like an eagle. Oh, they're wearing.
